prompt: I'm in a forecasting hackathon. We submit predictions after the close on day t and get scored on each stock's return from the close of t to the close of t+1. My teammate wrote features.py; sample data is in prices.csv and fundamentals.csv next to it. Can you audit it for look-ahead leakage, fix whatever is wrong, and save a corrected features_fixed.py (same build_features(prices, fundamentals) signature) plus a short audit_report.md that explains each problem and how you checked the fix?
assertions: Flags prices.dropna(axis=1) as survivorship/look-ahead (drops tickers using missing data from the future)
Flags prices.bfill() as filling gaps with future prices
Flags the momentum z-score normalised with full-sample mean/std
Flags rev.rank(pct=True) as ranking over the time axis (uses future rows)
Flags the centered rolling volatility window (center=True)
Flags the high-vol regime threshold taken from the full-sample quantile
Flags weekly momentum reindexed with method='bfill' (Friday's value used earlier in the week)
Flags fundamentals merged on period_end instead of filing date (reference time vs availability)
features_fixed.py runs on the sample data and passes the grader's perturbation and truncation leak checks
Does not report the cross-sectional cs_move feature (rank axis=1) as a leak
The report describes a dynamic check of the fix (perturbing or truncating data after t)
